Page 215 contains the end of §47, all of §48 and the start of §49.

**§47, end: three triangular numbers T(x)·T(y) = T(z), with T(k) = k(k+1)/2.**
- The method from p.214 imposes px(y+1) = 2qz and qy(x+1) = p(z+1).
- Put a = 2q² − p². This gives x = (f − 2q²)/a and y = (p² − g)/a for any factorisation fg = 2pq(pq − a).
- Take p = 7, q = 5, so a = 2·25 − 49 = 1. Then fg = 70·34 = 2380 = 4·5·7·17.
- The second choice is f = 85, g = 28 (85·28 = 2380). This gives x = 85 − 50 = 35 and y = 49 − 28 = 21.
- Then T(35) = 35·18 = 630 and T(21) = 11·21 = 231.
- z = px(y+1)/(2q) = 7·35·22/10 = 539 = 7·7·11. The other condition gives the same value: qy(x+1)/p − 1 = 5·21·36/7 − 1 = 539.
- Check: T(539) = 539·270 = 145530 = 630·231 = 35·18·11·21.

**§48: integer solutions of a x² − b y² = A.**
- Euler first notes that a solution requires A = a f² − b g² for some integers f, g. This is really just the existence of one seed solution.
- Next, solve the Pell equation m² − ab n² = 1. Then (m² − ab n²)^λ = 1, so a x² − b y² = (a f² − b g²)(m² − ab n²)^λ.
- Factoring over irrationals gives x√a + y√b = (f√a + g√b)(m + n√ab)^λ.
- [my step] For λ = 1: (f√a + g√b)(m + n√ab) = (fm + b g n)√a + (gm + a f n)√b. So the new solution is x' = fm + bgn, y' = gm + afn, which is integral. Iterating gives integer solutions.
- Example: 3x² − y² = 2, with f = 1, g = ±1, and Pell solution (m, n) = (2, 1) for m² − 3n² = 1. Then x√3 + y = (√3 + 1)(2 + √3)^λ.
- For λ = 0, …, 4 this gives (x, y) = (1, 1), (3, 5), (11, 19), (41, 71), (153, 265).
- Both sequences are recurrent: u_{k+1} = 2m·u_k − u_{k−1} with 2m = 4.

**Remark on the Pell equation: families with an explicit solution of m² − D n² = 1, where D = ab.**
- Classical cases D = α² ± 1 and α² ± 2.
- New, more general cases:
  - D = α²β² ± β gives n = 2α, m = 2α²β ± 1.
  - D = α²β² ± 2β gives n = α, m = α²β ± 1.
- [my check] (2α²β ± 1)² − (α²β² ± β)·4α² = 1, and (α²β ± 1)² − (α²β² ± 2β)·α² = 1.

**§49 (begun): find p, q with (p² + 1)² + (q² + 1)² = □.**
- Use the Pythagorean parametrisation p² + 1 = x² − y², q² + 1 = 2xy, so the sum is (x² + y²)².
- Then p² = x² − y² − 1 and q² = 2xy − 1.
- Put p = x − z. Then 2xz − z² = y² + 1, so x = (z² + y² + 1)/(2z) (continued on p.216).
errors: §48: the stated necessary condition A = a f² − b g² is tautological; it only says a seed solution must exist. Euler does not address that the solutions may form several classes needing several seeds, nor negative λ. Here g = −1 gives (√3 − 1)(2 + √3) = √3 + 1, so it falls in the same class, which is harmless.

§48: when ab = α² + 1 the obvious m = α, n = 1 gives m² − ab n² = −1, not +1. Euler only lists this case as classical without values, so there is no error on the page, but the +1 solution there is (2α² + 1, 2α).
No arithmetic errors found on this page. All five λ-values, both recurrences and the triangular-number identity check out.
